earnings.title: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
highlights: GAAP (United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) net earnings of $172.4 million, or diluted earnings per share of $1.82 versus third quarter 2025 net earnings of $170.8 million, or $1.76 per diluted share.
Operating income for the current quarter increased 2% to $247.1 million versus $242.7 million for the third quarter 2025.

Segment gross revenue increased 20% from the prior-year period, reflecting an 11% increase in gross revenue per load, resulting from higher fuel surcharge revenue, customer rates and changes in mix of freight, and the 8% increase in volume.
Revenue per load excluding fuel surcharge revenue increased 2% year-over-year.
Total operating revenue for the current quarter was $3.68 billion compared with $3.05 billion for the third quarter 2025, an increase of 20%.

quotes.text: I want to thank our people for their unwavering commitment to serving our customers, operating safely and executing with excellence every day. Their discipline and focus enabled us to meet customer needs, improve our operations, and continue providing excellent service.

outlook: We expect our 2026 full year annual tax rate to be approximately 24.0%.

items.heading: Our business can be significantly impacted by economic conditions, customer business cycles, government policies, and seasonal factors.
Extreme or unusual weather conditions can disrupt our operations, impact freight volumes, and increase our costs, all of which could have a material adverse effect on our business results.

Our operations are subject to various environmental laws and regulations, including legislative and regulatory responses to climate change. Compliance with environmental requirements could result in significant expenditures and the violation of these regulations could result in substantial fines or penalties.
We depend on third parties in the operation of our business, particularly rail service providers, transportation equipment manufacturers, third party carriers and independent contractors.
Rapid changes in fuel costs could impact our periodic financial results.
Insurance and claims expenses could significantly reduce our earnings.
